Resolve one provenance-bearing effective model

## Scope

Assembly or load/refresh of the model used by one selected Project.

## Claim

Resolve the Project and applicable source frontier; obtain the protected base, currently activated Extension identities/revisions and Project Configuration. Validate carrier/schema versions, source freshness, references and the selected compatibility/override contract. Bind the candidate to exact observed base, activated Extension and Project Configuration inputs, each identified by revision and byte digest (or an equally exact immutable source reference). Verify that the Project Configuration carrier is admitted for the retained Project identity and override surface. Compose one complete candidate effective model, preserving source meanings and distinguishing additions from explicit overrides. Apply the declared precedence; unresolved precedence or an unauthorized override shall not be resolved by discovery order, filename order or guesswork.

## Details

Record which source supplied every effective value and which declaration permits each override. A cyclic reference is accepted or rejected according to its declared semantics, not a blanket cycle ban. Produce one versioned effective-model generation and its diagnostics, whether it is materialized for consumers or composed by the runtime. Recheck the exact observed input set immediately before selecting the generation; changed inputs return a stale-candidate condition for a new resolution, rather than publishing mixed observations. For refresh, retain the prior complete generation without silently presenting it as the new one, and report the rejection; whether new operations may continue using that prior generation or must pause is an explicit policy choice. An operation shall retain one model generation through its dependent validation/effects rather than mixing generations mid-operation, while preserving existing freshness/revalidation rules at effects. When no complete usable generation exists, model-dependent operations return an attributable unavailable condition under the existing admission rules. Triggering refresh and changing unsupported engine semantics are separate procedures. This Method creates no new source authority and does not modify the graph-view quartet.

# Summary

Localize engineering decisions and reuse shared policies

## Scope

Every new or changed PROGRAMMATIC implementation decision represented by an
implemented RMED Atom, across Requirements, Methods, Evaluations and Deliveries
and their descendant Scope Units.

## Claim

Localize each implemented RMED engineering decision in one owning module or
one cohesive package whenever practical. Many-to-many implementation relations
remain valid, but an unimplemented Atom receives no invented implementation
target. Split a decision across modules only for a genuine boundary and record
the concrete reason; do not hide dispersed behavior behind a facade. Apply
cross-cutting policies everywhere they are applicable through one shared
canonical implementation, such as a decorator or common boundary, rather than
duplicating the policy logic. A caller, adapter or router is not an
implementation owner unless it contains independent claim-specific logic.

## Details

- Treat an engineering decision from any implemented R, M, E or D Atom as an
  ownership obligation; this policy is not limited to Requirements and
  Deliveries.
- Prefer one owning module or one cohesive package for the decision's actual
  behavior, structure or evidence rule. Several RMED Atoms may share an owner,
  and one Atom may have several owners when the relation is genuinely
  many-to-many.
- Do not create a fake implementation relation for an Atom that is not
  implemented. A trace link, caller, dependency or facade alone is not
  claim-specific realization. A test does not own the behavior it merely
  exercises. A test module that materially implements an Evaluation Atom
  does own that Evaluation and cites its ID in the module header.
- Use a multi-module split only when a real responsibility, lifecycle, effect,
  interface, data or security boundary requires it. Name that reason and keep
  the resulting units cohesive; do not scatter logic merely to reduce a local
  size measurement.
- Implement a cross-cutting policy once at its canonical shared boundary and
  apply that implementation at every applicable owner. A decorator, shared
  helper or equivalent boundary may carry the policy. If copied policy logic
  exists, report its actual realizing modules and review the duplication;
  do not hide a real implementation site by labelling it a mere consumer.
- Callers, adapters, routers and orchestration layers remain consumers unless
  they contain independent logic that realizes part of the RMED Claim. Do not
  make them owners only because they invoke an owner.
- Cite implemented RMED Atoms only at actual owning source-module headers,
  including owning modules within a package. A package initializer or facade
  is not an implementation owner solely because it re-exports the behavior.
  Use the separate implementation-trace syntax decision, not a second format.

## Adoption notes

This is a Draft policy for review. It is not current authority, does not
supersede CA-M-403, CA-M-411 or CA-M-419, and must not be treated as an active
implementation gate until separately accepted and promoted.

Companion Draft: [module-start ownership citations](CA-M-draft-PROGRAMMATIC-STANDARD-ENG_DECISION--write-rmed-owner-citations-only-at-module-start.md).

# Summary

Establish explicit Term Definitions and staged CCE consistency checks

## Question

How were the seventeen-RMED CCE packet and its necessary consumers reconciled with the Current subject system and promoted?

## Scope

Source adoption of the original seventeen-RMED packet in CORE_META_MODEL, including the three previously promoted Methods, plus narrow compatibility updates to optional terminology consumers. This Analysis remains a provisional tracking Draft. Runtime, parser, generated-view publication, project-wide vocabulary migration and complete occurrence review are outside these source effects.

## Approach

Apply the Operator's latest decisions over older Draft text. Verify Current authority from Project Structure, rebase stale candidates without losing adopted metadata or formal constraints, independently review the new Subject bindings and semantic boundaries, allocate fresh identities under the canonical Project lock, archive actual Current predecessors and consume only the fourteen remaining packet Drafts. Record actual source effects independently in the Journal.

## Results

### Accepted model

Each reusable Term has one explicit authoritative R/Term Definition. M explains writing its content; E checks well-formedness and consistent use in stages: entity names, Claim, Claim Scope, Semantics, Details and remaining authored fields. D carries content and review evidence through existing carriers. No dictionary Projection or lookup service is a prerequisite.

Complete canonical entity names retain one-to-one bindings and exact authored usage. `atom.id` and `projection.id` are distinct complete qualified property names using the same ID meaning; their terminal component need not be globally unique. ID means a unique identifier used to find an entity instance across Continuant and Occurrent instances, with uniqueness within matching prefix namespaces. The supplied version/state-qualified identifier examples do not independently establish lifecycle equivalence or a general case-folding rule.

`Package` is reused in `Package`, `Eval Package` and `Runtime Package`; `Unit` in `Scope Unit` and `Code Unit`. The chain `Package > Module > Code Unit` connects three entities without a fourth chain entity. Qualification syntax, explicit definitions and source identity remain separate. Ordinary words, property labels, instance labels and path spelling do not automatically become Project Terms or defining authority.

### New subject system and resolved lexical binding

Current authority uses the `Entity` root with Object, Aspect, Graph Syntax and Carrier branches. References use admitted `/`, `//`, `.`, `:`, `>`, existing-kind `@(...)` and named-relation syntax. The old `Subject/CAPRMEDIO/...` paths and unsupported `::` notation were removed from operative packet references. RMED bodies now use Current CA-D-479@25 sibling headings: Summary, optional Claim scope, Claim, optional Semantics and Details; required formal constraints in existing sources were preserved.

**Q-TERM-TARGET is resolved from Current authority.** CA-R-1318 establishes the Term kind; CA-R-2229 establishes the distinct Term Definition Type; CA-R-1194@29 permits a defining Atom to introduce its target; CA-R-1931@15 and CA-R-2002@15 admit named-instance `K//Name` syntax. Parsing property names does not create it, invent Unit/domain objects or implement a Terms Graph. Existing Term placement is not reclassified.

The Type Draft was merged into existing CA-R-2229, not allocated as a duplicate Type. Entity Definition of the Term kind remains distinct from lexical Term Definition ownership; the former does not silently grant Governed Term status to every word in its text.

### Post-review Property decisions

The Operator resolves the concept question by using Property as the single canonical Term for the former Property/Dependent Entity distinction. The Claim describes a Property whose identity requires its immediate bearer, connected through IS_PROPERTY_OF. The root, structural, lexical and registered consumer Drafts now use `Entity/Property` and `Entity/Term//Property`. The earlier separate-kind preparations are withdrawn from this active register. The reviewed 112-Draft frontier remains an immutable historical review snapshot; it does not certify these later changes.

The Operator assigns these statements to the indicated content sections:

| Statement | Placement / disposition |
|---|---|
| Exactly one immediate bearer | Formal claim, using `Property {1}((IS_PROPERTY_OF)) Bearer` under the latest two-sided Relation convention. |
| No separate Carrier of the Property's own | Claim. |
| No directed IS_PROPERTY_OF cycles, including self-loops | Structural Property Claim; checked by E449. Other Relation Types remain separately governed. |
| Applicable direct-value Format and cardinality | Claim; exactly one bearer does not imply exactly one value. |
| A Property may itself be a bearer | Semantics; nested Properties, including a possible Status Property, remain permitted. |
| Additional bearer-qualified-identity clause | Not required by this Property definition. |
| Generic prohibition on independent lifecycle / compulsory update rule | Not adopted; the definition does not ban `bearer.property.status`. |

The shared `{cardinality}` syntax has different counted domains. In `property[format]{cardinality}` it counts direct Property values, with `[format]` declaring their Format. The latest `Source {forward-count}((RELATION_TOKEN)){reverse-count} Target` form counts Relation instances in each direction independently: forward per Source, reverse per Target. Each Relation connects two nodes or node instances; neither count is Relation arity or a distinct-target count. `Property {1}((IS_PROPERTY_OF)) Bearer` leaves the reverse count unspecified, so nested Properties remain permitted. R1931 and R2243 record this distinction. The expression is schematic, not an edge asserted between kind nodes.

The Operator explicitly approved **IS_PROPERTY_OF with derived inverse HAS_PROPERTY**. The new Relation Definitions receive fresh unallocated R identities because renaming a Summary cannot repurpose the old Relation's identity. Store the direct fact once; derive the inverse without an independent reverse fact. Current IS_BORNE_BY/BEARS sources remain untouched and are historical predecessors, not aliases for the proposed names.

The Operator approved prohibiting directed IS_PROPERTY_OF cycles, including self-loops. Exactly one outgoing Relation per Property alone would permit two Properties to be each other's bearer, so this is a separate structural constraint in R1193's Claim. E449 checks self-loops, mutual and longer bearer cycles, while preserving valid nested Property chains. The rule does not constrain value references or other Relation Types. The consolidation resolves the Property/Dependent Entity distinction; classification-grammar adoption and other findings from the full review remain pending.

## Summary

Notation baseline for intuitive symbol review

## Question

Which short keyboard notations make these meanings easiest to read correctly?

## Scope

Latest Operator-agreed meanings, including Draft changes. Latest human input
supersedes earlier wording. This is review input, not Current adoption or
evidence of parser support.

## Approach

Use this baseline explicitly; do not infer meanings from other languages.
The Astra-max comparison is complete. The Operator then selected the
Composition and Classification spellings below and clarified two-sided
Relation cardinality. Use compact English-keyboard symbols while balancing
visual readability and intuitive understanding. No qualification replacement
has been selected; `/`, `()` and `.` retain their meanings.

## Results

### Meaning baseline

| Notation | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `X/Y` | Y is narrower than X and inherits X's applicable features and constraints. |
| `Part +> Whole` | Part is part of Whole. The pointer faces the Whole; containment supplies no inheritance. |
| `Whole <+ Part` | Whole has Part: the reverse written view of the same containment fact. The pointer still faces the Whole. |
| `X >\| Y` | X has Classification Y. The pointer faces the Classification endpoint, marked by the bar. This is axis applicability, not membership in a particular group. |
| `Y \|< X` | Y is the Classification applicable to X: the reverse written view of the same fact. |
| `X.Y` | Y is a Property borne by X. |
| `X: Y` | Y is an allowed value of X, regardless of X's kind or preceding path. This is not assignment and does not imply that X is a Property. |
| `X/(.Y: Z)` | An X qualified by its own Property Y and allowed value Z. The qualified X inherits from X; Y does not become a subtype of X. |
| `K//Name` | The named instance Name of kind K, not a narrower kind. |
| `[format]` | Declared Format of a Property's direct values. |
| `x.y[format]{cardinality}` | Format and count of the Property's direct values: `{n}` exactly n, `{n+}` at least n, `{n..m}` inclusive range. |
| `Source {f}RELATION{r} Target` | Two independent directional counts: f constrains links from each Source toward Target; r constrains reverse links from each Target toward Source. An omitted side is unspecified. These do not count Relation arity. |
| `@` | Call/reference to an already declared Entity; it does not declare a new Entity. |
| `()` | Logical grouping of the enclosed expression, including relative Property qualification. |
| `Source ((RELATION_TYPE)) Target` | A named Relation with its declared direction and endpoints. The double-parenthesis form is a distinct compound notation. |

### Examples and boundaries

```text
Atom.Status >| Status Group: Draft <+ Draft
Atom.Status >| Status Group: Archived <+ Archived
Atom.Status >| Status Group: Current <+ * not in (Draft, Archived)

Step {1}+>{1+} Workflow
Workflow {1+}<+{1} Step
```

Status Group classifies Atom Status values. Each group contains the Status
values shown on its right. `*` ranges only over admitted Atom Status values.
These three groups are mutually exclusive and exhaustive within that domain.
The wildcard mapping is Formal claim text; it does not introduce an executable
Boolean or query grammar for Subjects.

The last two lines are equivalent: each Step belongs to exactly one Workflow,
and each Workflow has one or more Steps. Reversing the written direction
swaps the two count positions. Missing counts remain unspecified; property
value counts remain separate. This supersedes the former Relation convention
where a single postfix count always counted outgoing links from the left.

`Atom/(.Type: Method)` denotes the whole qualified Atom, which inherits from
Atom. This notation example alone does not admit Method as a Type value;
the admitted Content Role example is `Atom/(.Content Role: Method)`.

Containment retains direct IS_CONTAINED_BY and derived CONTAINS.
`>|` retains HAS_CLASSIFICATION, and `|<` is its selected reverse view.
Choosing that view introduces no separately authored reverse fact or new
canonical inverse Relation Type name. The selected spellings replace bare
`>` / `<` containment and the earlier `::` axis spelling. The selected
Composition pointer faces the Whole, superseding the opposite direction in
the FPF report's earlier conditional `+>` candidate; that report stays unchanged.

### Authorized adoption and migration

The Operator requests: update/review/fix the full Term/Property proposal,
promote the reviewed closed batch to Active, then migrate Current notation.
The scope includes the 125-Draft packet and required notation owners; it
preserves the accepted Property relation and Method-owned Term definitions.

Classification is not a new Entity kind. HAS_CLASSIFICATION and
IS_CLASSIFIED_BY are named Relation instances under Graph Syntax; a generic
Classification word definition, if needed, belongs to Terms. No inverse pair
is inferred merely from listing those two Relation names.

Review and repair stale successors from their live Current owners before
promotion. Use the admitted lifecycle/identity-allocation path, preserve
archived/history bytes, migrate only reviewed expressions, update parser and
consumers together, and rebuild derived projections. A source/promotion
record alone does not establish implementation or migration success.

### Source alignment

The table incorporates generic `:`, `@` for an already declared Entity,
logical grouping `()`, the selected symbol pairs and two-sided Relation
cardinality. The repaired full proposal now has a 130-Draft adoption closure,
including the 125-Draft register and five required notation owners. Older
Current wording remains migration work; it does not override the latest human
decisions. Draft preparation does not establish Current adoption.

Approved AST support and its graph, lookup and validator callers are prepared
in source. Ten focused parser tests pass. Installed runtime activation,
Current publication and migration have not occurred. Broader test runs have
separate filesystem limits; they are not an all-green certification.

[HAS_CLASSIFICATION](../../04_requirement/draft/classification-and-status-groups/CA-R-draft-CORE_META_MODEL-RELATION_DEFINITION--define-has-classification.md),
and [Format/cardinality](../../04_requirement/draft/CA-R-2243@3-draft-CORE_META_MODEL-ENTITY_DEFINITION--define-cardinality-notation.md).

## TLDR

The selected pairs are `Part +> Whole / Whole <+ Part` and
`X >| Y / Y |< X`. Relation counts constrain both directions independently;
Property value counts stay postfix. Source parser checks pass; adoption and
Current notation migration remain pending actual lifecycle execution.

# Summary

Define Value Constraint Annotations

## Claim

A [format, condition] annotation specifies the format of each direct property value and an additional condition on it. Its expressions are interpreted as materialized values or value domains needed for checking the annotation. An explicit execute_selection() or materialization call is not required in this context.

For a named Selection followed by a member property, materialize the Selection's result and obtain that property from each selected member. Thus Selection//All Scope Unit.Name supplies the selected Scope Unit names, not the Selection entity's own Name. The membership condition uses those resulting strings. A lower-bound condition >=1 requires the direct numeric value to be at least one.

This value context does not change the independent cardinality suffix, count nested keys, make @ itself a materialization operator, or redefine ordinary Model-property paths outside the annotation.

### Formal claim

```text
atom.version_number[int, >=1]
atom.scope_owner[string, in Selection//All Scope Unit.Name]
```

## Semantics

Named selections define their result population. The format-and-condition annotation makes clear that the population's values are being used rather than its graph identity. Materialization here describes obtaining values for the check; it does not prescribe persistence or create new model entities.

## Details

A1291 records the Operator decision. The owner expression is an illustrative logical property path, not a YAML field rename or an automatically registered Selection. This prepared Definition does not implement a parser or evaluator or promote general formula/function syntax.

# Summary

List Logical Content Fields

## Claim

The proposed read-only `content.get_list()` function, applied to an Atom kind, qualified kind, or selected Atom instance, returns registered Markdown Content headings. For a kind it returns allowed registered headings, including applicable inherited and optional headings. For a selected instance it returns only headings actually present.

The registered headings are `# Summary`, optional `## Claim scope`, `## Claim`, optional `## Semantics`, and optional `## Details`. The function returns heading names, not heading values, logical-key aliases, function names, or unrelated metadata. `atom.content.details` returns the text/value under the registered Details heading. Formal and natural claims both use `atom.content.claim`; version identity remains `atom.version_number` in YAML.

This proposal does not add `atom.property`, colon/property-text layers, or any other API. `atom.get_properties()` is a separate proposal for the full property set, including Content, with exact return shape unresolved. Existing Summary content remains unchanged.

## Details

The proposal distinguishes allowed headings for a kind from actual headings present in a selected instance. It remains separate from Formal Claim syntax and does not authorize parser, Tool, runtime, Current-source, or projection changes.

## Proposal status

This is a proposed candidate only, tracked by CA-A-1237. Its normative wording is not adopted methodology and must not be promoted as part of relation-notation changes.

# Summary

Require Unique Primary Kind Names

## Scope

Primary-kind declarations in the effective Subject model, including shared and project-local branches.

## Claim

Distinct primary-kind declarations **must** have unique canonical names across the effective Subject model. An existing-kind reference **may** use that name inside `@(...)`, as in `@(Module)`, and **must** resolve to exactly one declared kind. Repeated references to the same kind are not new declarations. An ambiguous name **must not** be resolved by choosing a branch or merging distinct targets.

## Semantics

This is declaration-name uniqueness, not uniqueness of every raw path component or every displayed occurrence. Property names may repeat under different bearers; classification-axis names and allowed values remain qualified by their existing rules. Instance naming remains governed within its kind and is not made globally unique by this rule. Escaping changes representation, not the intended kind's name.

A branch move alone leaves a unique-name reference valid. A primary-name rename requires reference migration. A current full canonical path may still identify the same kind; retired paths do not become aliases. No alias registry is introduced.

## Details

This Draft records the Operator's explicit Yes to Q07 in CA-A-1236. Existing distinct same-label kinds, including Aspect Documentation and actual Implementation Documentation, require a reviewed naming correction before this rule can be applied across Current sources. This Draft does not perform those renames or implement lookup. No numeric Atom ID is allocated until promotion preparation.

The proposed `content.get_list()` contract must distinguish allowed registered Markdown Content headings for a kind from headings actually present in a selected instance. It must return heading names, not heading values, logical-key aliases, unrelated metadata keys, or function names.
